subject: Sample size and effect sizes compare.pls

messages.author: 9593a45d774ba566
messages.subject: Sample size and effect sizes compare.pls
parts:
Hello,
I'm trying to use the compare.pls function to compare the strength of integration of traits between three different species. For two of these species (HC & DE), my sample size is around 30 individuals, and for the third (HV), over 100 individuals. I am aware that, according to "On the comparison of the strength of morphological integration across morphometric datasets", the use of Rpls values is dependant on sample size, so I am using the recommended compare.pls function to compare the strength of integration between these three species. However, I want to make sure I'm interpreting the compare.pls output correctly because these results (in particular the effect sizes) also seem to depend on the sample size. 

If I run compare.pls with the 3 full datasets, then we get effect sizes (the $sample.z object) of: 

HV    3.334794          DE 1.365760          HC  1.930840 

If, however, I run compare.pls for HC & DE plus reduced dataset with a random sample of 30 rows from HV, then the effect size for HV is very different. 

HVRed 0.8437519                  DE 1.3657602       HC 1.9308398  
                                             
So this effect size is apparently dependent on sample size. Is that as it should be? I think I may have misunderstood from the paper what exactly this effect size is, and whether it should or should not vary with sample size. Is it rather the $pairwise.z object that is less affected by sample size? For what it's worth, this doesn't change the inference based on p-values in the compare.pls output.

My data are attached. The code I used was:
#
DEint<-integration.test(A=DE,partition.gp=c(rep("adv",7),rep("agg",7)),iter=1000,seed=NULL)
HCint<-integration.test(A=HC,partition.gp=c(rep("adv",8),rep("agg",8)),iter=1000,seed=NULL)
HVint<-integration.test(A=HV,partition.gp=c(rep("adv",5),rep("agg",6)),iter=1000,seed=NULL)
HVReducedint<-integration.test(A=HVRed,partition.gp=c(rep("adv",5),rep("agg",6)),iter=1000,seed=NULL)

fullcompare<-compare.pls(DEint,HCint,HVint)
Reducedcompare<-compare.pls(DEint,HCint,HVReducedint)
#

Note that these are phenotypic traits but not morphological landmarks, and that I measured a few different traits for each species (but these traits still fall into the two proposed modules).

Thanks for any advice!

Michael Reichert
